title: Performance Review Cycle
description: HR and managers: run review rounds with goals, feedback and sign-off.

spec.useCase: Valentina Rossi leads people at a sixty-person software company and uses this to run each review cycle without a spreadsheet.

business.name: Bright Harbor Technologies
business.describes: A sixty-person software company running two review cycles a year.

tables.name: Review cycles
tables.describes: Each review round with its dates, status and how many reviews are complete.
tables.subject: thing

tables.name: Reviews
tables.describes: One review per person per cycle, from self-review through to delivery.
tables.subject: thing

independentOf.cycle: A review is due on its own date, set by the manager within the review window.
independentOf.employee: Anyone can be reviewed whenever they joined.

tables.name: Goals
tables.describes: The goals each person committed to, how far along they are and whether they are on track.
tables.subject: thing

independentOf.owner: Any employee can own a goal.
independentOf.review: A goal is due on its own date, not the review's.

values.goal_name: Cut median reply time to 2 hours

tables.describes: Written feedback about a person from peers, managers and reports.
tables.subject: thing

independentOf.about: Anyone can give feedback to anyone.
independentOf.review: Feedback is given when the giver chooses, not tied to a review date.

text.text: Run each review round from one page: reviews moving through stages, goals with progress, and feedback collected along the way.
Reviews by stage
Review cycles
Goals
Feedback
Rubric
Open the Rating rubric page before calibration; every rating needs one example.
These numbers update as you work. Use this page for the weekly check, then open the list behind any number to act on it.
Needs attention
Reviews due next
How to read this page
Each chart groups your entries as shown; click a slice to see the entries behind it.
The lists below show only what needs attention now.
If a chart looks off, check that every entry is connected to the right person or item.
Use the same scale for self, manager and final ratings.
Calibration compares ratings across managers. Bring one example for any 1, 2 or 5.
Using the rubric
Rate the work, not the person, and name the evidence.
Compare against the role expectations, not against colleagues.
If self and manager ratings differ by two or more, schedule a conversation before delivering.
